Yes, but it is much more manageable to deal with the consequences. The game has various mission types that pop up occasionally. Guerrilla Missions are the ones that have replaced earlier mission types in terms of consequences. They appear only once per month as opposed to multiple times.

Narratively, the way they work is that the organization receives intel to disrupt some of the aliens' activities, and you can choose where to strike. If you do not make a choice, the aliens will complete the activity they are working towards. The organization can only strike in regions they control, and a maximum of three missions will appear at once, requiring you to choose one.

As you might expect, if the aliens finish their activity, it will negatively impact you. This is referred to as a Dark Event. There are several types of Dark Events, and they are randomly selected. Some include:

All enemy forces gain one armor for a month; enemy raids make new recruits cost double for a month; enemy awareness increases, making stealth tactics nearly useless for a month.

You can see beforehand which events are which and then choose which one you want to prevent the most. However, the consequences of the Dark Events, while certainly noticeable, are very minor compared to earlier versions of the game.

If, theoretically, all Dark Events occurred, it still wouldn't be a huge deal, especially if you are somewhat skilled at the game. At that point, one more point of armor doesn't really matter, and having a reinforcement pod on every mission for a month doesn't significantly impact gameplay.

This is a real tactics game. I love tactical RPGs but that is much more of a puzzle game than anything else.

1. **Never dash**. If you uncover a new group of enemies and you can't move anymore you'll have a bad time. The only exception is if you're concealed.

2. **Optimize your actions**. This means you take one action with every unit (and check their options) and only after that take the final action with each one. Imagine moving a unit and having a 25% and 45% chance to hit and you take the 45% one and miss. Then you move another unit and realize he has a 100% chance to hit on the 45% target. Bad order. The correct way is to move the first unit, see the 45%, then move the second unit, see the 100% so take that shot and then switch back to either take the 25% shot or go on overwatch or something else.

3. **Increase your chances to hit**. By setting up flanks, removing cover with explosives and abilities, taking high ground and modifying your weapons. If the average chance to hit you have is 70% and their average to hit you is 50% you should generally win because you hit/kill them way more.

4. **Care about your unit's survival**. The best defense means eliminating everything before they have a chance to retaliate. If not possible though, or if it won't work, plan to keep your units safe. Learn enemy behavior and damage amounts.
